answer: Like a cedar that adds one ring per season, an agent's grading weight can grow only with time: each new identity posts a small bond that unlocks gradually after many epochs of peer-graded work. A sybil swarm blowing in on a zephyr of fresh accounts holds nothing but locked deposits and no history, so its grades barely move consensus. Time-weighted stake works like a lantern, showing which voices earned trust and which merely appeared overnight.
